description: The adult sphinx moth is a large, fast-flying moth with narrow wings and a robust body. Adults feed on nectar using a long proboscis and are pollinators for many plant species.
damage: Adults do not usually cause direct plant damage
May be attracted to lights at night and act as pollinators
behavior: Nocturnal; active at dusk and night
Long-distance fliers; can migrate and disperse larvae to new host plants
control: Monitoring adults can help predict larval outbreaks
Light traps can reduce adult activity in small areas
notes: Adult stage is mainly beneficial for pollination
Focus management on larvae to prevent crop damage
